text:
Mara K.: Quick heads-up — seeing a 12-18% tail latency regression on AWQ INT8 (weight-only) after the recent kernel selector change. Only shows up for group-size=128 on the rtxa-gpu pool. Perf harness attached below. :warning:

Deven: Can you paste the exact bench command and the perf summary? wanted to repro locally.

Mara K.: Ran microbench with the continuous-batcher harness:`./bench --model meta/gpt-7b-awq --quant awq --group 128 --batch 1 --seq 128 --kv-cache true --runtime rtxa`

Perf snippet (nvprof / microprof):
```
kernel: int8_gemm_pack -> int8_gemm_unpack (fallback path)
p50: 22.1ms -> 26.3ms
p95: 86.4ms -> 102.7ms
tokens/sec: 420 -> 369
avg packing overhead: +11.2ms per request
memcpy (pack) increased by 3.6ms, unpack by 4.8ms
KV cache hit path: unchanged
```

Jyoti: Interesting — that pack->unpack swap smells like the selector is choosing the alignment-unfriendly kernel for group 128. AWQ calibrator sometimes marks groups as "misaligned" if calibration sigmas exceed threshold and forces the safe kernel. Did calibration stats change recently?

Mara K.: Calibration artifacts look similar to before. I suspect the recent "kernel-fallback on small-blocks" guard landed in selector (PR #4821) is too aggressive for certain weight layouts. The fallback adds an extra pack/unpack roundtrip inside the kernel, hence the ~11ms hit. This mostly affects short-inference latency; long loops amortize it because pack cost is per-request.

Deven: Repro steps confirmed here. Quick local numbers: group=128 p95 101ms, group=64 p95 93ms, group=32 p95 89ms. So smaller groups reduce fallback incidence but also hurt compression/quant error — need to balance.

Jyoti: From calibration runs: group128 has ~0.8% extra MSE vs fp16 (acceptable), group64 drops MSE by ~0.2%. But AWQ remaps some blocks into fallback if quant-error > 0.9% (config: awq.calib.fallback_threshold). Try bumping threshold to 1.2% as an experiment.

Liam: Quick runtime tweak that helped on my end: enable prefer_packed_kernels in selector-config and add an alignment relaxation when seq_len%8==0. Patch diff: `selector->prefer_packed = true; if ((seq_len & 7)==0) prefer_packed = true;` Not pretty but reduced fallback rate on our bench. Also try the pack-simd build (ENABLE_PACK_SIMD=1).

Mara K.: Ran two experiments: 1) set awq.calib.fallback_threshold=1.2% => p95 down from 102.7ms to 94.5ms, tokens/sec up to 395. 2) prefer_packed_kernels + alignment relaxation => p95 90.2ms, tokens/sec 412.

Deven: Good signal. Any downside? Quality regressions?

Jyoti: For threshold bump, small delta in perplexity on eval set (+0.35) — within the monitoring tolerance but we should run full evals. For selector relaxation, we risk picking a packed kernel that misbehaves on rare layouts; need a safety-check in runtime to validate outputs for first N tokens (sanity checksum) before committing to route.

Mara K.: Agreed. Action items:
- [ ] Jyoti to run full AWQ eval suite with fallback_threshold=1.2 (PERF-423)
- [ ] Eng-runtime to prototype runtime checksum validation and a fast fallback counter (Mara/Deven)
- [ ] Add a short-sequence routing rule to choose non-AWQ (or GPTQ variant) for latencies <200ms until selector fix deployed

perf-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-15T18:12:41 UTC rolled kernel-selector:v1.9.2 -> v1.9.3 (sha: abcdef). Noted 2/3 canaries show +10% p95 on rtxa pool.

Liam: I'll open a kernel-selector revert PR and also a targeted patch to relax the small-block guard.

Mara K.: Thanks — putting a dashboard card for short sequences and adding a perf test in CI that runs group-size sweep (32/64/128) across kernels so this doesn't regress silently. :memo: :mag:

Deven: Adding notes to the postmortem template and linking the bench scripts: `scripts/bench/awq_group_sweep.sh`

Jyoti: FYI: this explains some customer reports about higher latency on short completions this morning. Will notify CS with a short blurb. :phone:

Mara K.: Cool — keep updates here. If someone wants to reproduce quickly: I pushed the microbench container `redwood/bench:awq-pulse-2026` on the canary pool.`:eyes:
